title: Poisson braisé à la camerounaise (with Sauce Essaho)
author: Amina Savoura (Afrik.com) — recipe by cocobig2002 (Beauté d’Afrik)
desc: Per-person recipe: a bream scored and brushed with a fried paste of chilli, djanssan, ginger, onion, tomato and celery, grilled about 15 minutes a side, with a soy-and-sesame sauce essaho.
longDesc: Quantities are given per person. The fish is scaled, gutted, gills and fins removed, head and tail left on, and lightly scored and salted. The chilli, djanssan, ginger (djidja), celery, onion and tomato are crushed with salt and fried about 15 minutes in the oil; the fish is brushed with the paste and left about ten minutes. It is grilled over a barbecue or under the oven grill about 15 minutes per side, brushed again, and garnished with parsley. The sauce essaho (bouillon, onions and garlic, hot sauce, black soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil, salt, white pepper) is listed, but the page stops at ‘Portez à ébullition… Baissez le feu, laissez frémir’ — its method is incomplete.
ingredients: Onions and garlic — quantities not printed
1 tablespoon hot sauce or small chillies
A pinch of freshly ground white pepper
1 medium sea bream (about 300 g) or 1 sea bass
steps: Scale and gut the fish, remove the gills and fins, leaving the head and tail. Score lightly, salt and pepper.
Crush the chilli, djanssan, ginger, celery, onion and tomato with salt. Fry in the oil about 15 minutes.
Brush the fish with the paste and leave about ten minutes.
Grill over a barbecue or under the oven grill about 15 minutes per side, brushing again. Garnish with parsley.
Sauce essaho: the page lists the ingredients and says to bring to the boil and lower the heat to simmer, but gives no further method.
chefTips: The page prints no doneness cue; check the thickest part for flesh that flakes.
Quantities are per person — scale up for more fish.
The sauce essaho method is incomplete as printed.
commonMistakes: Not leaving head and tail on as the page says.
Expecting a complete sauce method — the page stops short.
healthBenefits: Fish with an oil-and-spice paste; the sauce adds sugar and salt.
culturalNote: The page title attributes the dish to Cameroon only. The recipe is credited to ‘cocobig2002 sur Beauté d’Afrik’ and the page byline is Amina Savoura.
sources: Title as printed: ‘Poisson braisé à la camerounaise’. Byline as printed: ‘Amina Savoura’; credit ‘Une recette de cocobig2002 sur Beauté d’Afrik’. ‘Publié le 24 septembre 2012 à 06h36’. Quantities ‘par personne’. TWO-PASS.

INCOMPLETE METHOD, stated plainly: the sauce essaho has ingredients but no method; two stray lines ‘Portez à ébullition’ and ‘Baissez le feu, laissez frémir’ appear unattached. ABSENT: oven temperature; doneness cue; onion and garlic quantities for the sauce.
